name: Leukocyte Chemotactic Factor 2 Amyloidosis

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of amyloid deposits in tissue biopsy with Congo red staining showing apple-green birefringence under polarized light
Immunohistochemical or mass spectrometry identification of LECT2 protein in amyloid deposits
Exclusion of other types of amyloidosis such as AL or AA by immunohistochemistry or genetic testing
Presence of clinical features consistent with ALECT2 amyloidosis such as renal impairment and/or hepatic involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histological confirmation of amyloid deposits with Congo red staining plus identification of LECT2 protein in deposits and exclusion of other amyloidosis types
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for LECT2 mutations is not typically diagnostic as the disease is considered acquired.

occasional.symptomName: Abnormality of multiple cell lineages in the bone marrow

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen indicating renal impairment
Normal or mildly elevated liver function tests
imaging: Ultrasound showing enlarged kidneys with increased echogenicity
Abdominal ultrasound or CT showing hepatomegaly
Echocardiogram may show restrictive cardiomyopathy in rare cases
genetic: No consistent pathogenic mutations identified; disease considered acquired
other: Tissue biopsy with Congo red staining demonstrating apple-green birefringence
Mass spectrometry or immunohistochemistry confirming LECT2 protein in amyloid deposits

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of monoclonal light chains in serum or urine
Different clinical context and laboratory markers

redFlags: Signs of cardiac amyloidosis such as restrictive cardiomyopathy
references: Sethi S, Theis JD, Vrana JA, et al. Leukocyte chemotactic factor 2 amyloidosis (ALECT2): a review. Amyloid. 2017;24(3):157-163.
Dasari S, Theis JD, Vrana JA, et al. Leukocyte chemotactic factor 2 amyloidosis: a case series and review of the literature. Amyloid. 2015;22(3):157-161.
